h: Beyond the garden gate in Wester Ross
p: Two or three hours is a good starting point for Inverewe, though garden lovers can easily stretch that. Out here distances are bigger than they look on the map and some roads are single-track with passing places, so build in a bit of slack and don't plan your day to the minute.

Loch Ewe has a remarkable wartime story. During the Second World War it was a gathering point for the Arctic convoys that carried supplies to the Soviet Union through brutal northern seas. Up the road at Aultbea, the Russian Arctic Convoy Museum tells that story, and it's a moving add-on if you've got the time.

Head south-west and you're soon in Gairloch, with sandy beaches, a harbour and a good local museum, while Loch Maree, one of the most beautiful lochs in the Highlands, stretches away inland. Carry on past it and you'll reach the Beinn Eighe National Nature Reserve near Kinlochewe, with trails through ancient pinewoods.

Poolewe sits on the North Coast 500 route, so you'll share the roads with plenty of road-trippers in the busy months. Fill up with fuel when you get the chance, pack midge repellent for summer evenings and keep snacks in the car. Do all that and this stretch of coast will reward you with some of the finest scenery in the country.
